reaction.notes:
Use this file ONLY if 'applies_if' tokens are present.
Then try base_rules (top→down). If none match, use default_rule.
After picking a rule, scan all modifiers and apply those that match (tokens OR plain‑text heuristics).
Notes: Ullmann/Goldberg systems are sensitive to base/solubility and mass transfer. Start with 5–10 mol% Cu(I) (CuI or Cu2O) and 10–40 mol% ligand (2–4× Cu). Use 2–3 equiv carbonate/phosphate base, ~10 vol solvent, 0.1–0.3 M, 90–110 °C for Ar–Br/I (110–130 °C for harder cases). Inert atmosphere preferred; modest water (5–10 equiv) can improve heterogeneous bases.

default_rule.description: General starter for Ullmann/Goldberg C–N (CuI or Cu2O; amino‑acid or diamine ligand; carbonate base).

conditions.solvent: Dioxane or toluene (alt: DMSO/DMF for polar substrates)
additives: Optional 5–10 equiv H2O to aid heterogeneous bases

base_rules.name: Primary/secondary aliphatic amines
base_rules.description: Broad coupling of primary/secondary aliphatic amines. Diamines excel for less nucleophilic or hindered cases.

conditions.solvent: Toluene or dioxane (alt: DMSO for polar cases)

base_rules.name: Anilines and less hindered amines
base_rules.description: Economical first pass; amino‑acid ligands promote rate and robustness.

base_rules.name: Heteroaromatic N–H (indoles, imidazoles, benzimidazoles)
base_rules.description: Phenanthroline‑type ligands often enable milder temps and higher selectivity with azoles.

base_rules.name: Goldberg amidation (amides and sulfonamides)
base_rules.description: Low‑nucleophilicity N; diamines or simple amino‑acids are effective.

base_rules.name: Aryl chlorides (Cu, challenging)
base_rules.description: Use oxalamide (or NHC/Cu) systems; higher temp and strong base often required.

base_rules.name: Ammonia as N‑source
base_rules.description: Direct arylation of NH3; consider oxalamide or robust diamine ligands.

base_rules.name: Hindered secondary aliphatic amines
base_rules.description: Ligand systems such as DMPAO (Ma) enable milder temps for historically tough aliphatic secondary amines.

when: symptom:heterogeneous base (carbonate/phosphate) or scale‑up in apolar solvent
modifiers.suggest: Add 5–10 equiv H2O or switch to a more polar co‑solvent to improve mass transfer.
Use diamine ligand (DMEDA/DMCyDA), raise temperature toward 110–120 °C, and choose Cs2CO3.
Switch to phenanthroline‑type ligands (DMPhen) and toluene; temps can often drop to 60–90 °C.
Use oxalamide (or NHC/Cu) ligands with K3PO4 in dioxane; plan 110–130 °C.
Run under N2/Ar; many systems tolerate trace air/moisture, but inert handling improves reproducibility.
Increase dilution (12–15 vol), add a polar co‑solvent (DMSO/DMF), or warm pre‑mix to dissolve salts.
Increase Cu/ligand loading slightly (e.g., +2–3 mol% Cu), use diamine or phenanthroline ligand, and consider more polar solvent.
Add 5–10 equiv water, reduce base particle size, or switch to partially soluble base to shorten induction.
Reactivity typically follows Ar–I ≫ Ar–Br » Ar–Cl. For bromides/iodides, try 90–110 °C; for chlorides, use oxalamide/NHC systems.
